items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: And also, the relationship of Sun Yat-sen was inspired by Lincoln.

ctx.x: Well I understand what you’re — I understand your question, because you’re inferring about whether music has programmatic aspects to it. Or at least that’s one part of it. That’s not necessarily the whole part. But I would say that sometimes these titles, they come through me at the particular time. So “River of Life” is actually from Revelation and after 9/11 the pastor, a woman pastor, offered the Scripture. And it was very — the Bible has very poetic scriptures. And one of the last lines is that leaves are for…

progressives, social democrats, liberals, Roosevelt-new dealers — it was a kind of a united front or a coalition. And of course you know about, because of that movement, you know Roosevelt created the Works Progress Administration, which provided work for artists, you know, and sometimes labor union contexts. And Aaron Copland wanted to — one of his musical goals was that we need to change the music so that it would become more accessible to the public. Because the public was alienated by sort of the you know,…
